jobs.title: Associate Director, CRM Platforms & Data Governance
jobs.description:
About Us

SickKids Foundation, with over 50 years of philanthropic impact is Canada's largest charitable funder of child health research, learning and care, raising over $200 million last year. As a national charity, SickKids Foundation invests in national and international initiatives to benefit children in Canada and around the world. As the fundraising partner to The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids), we are aligned in supporting Precision Child Health (PCH), the future of tailoring medicine to each child's unique traits so SickKids can diagnose faster, treat smarter, and predict better.

We are driven by our core values of integrity, collaboration, excellence, innovation, and inclusion, with goals of delivering a superior donor experience, investing in our people and culture, driving innovative and sustainable fundraising, and disrupting the market through data and technology.

SickKids Foundation is committed to an inclusive culture by embedding equity, diversity and inclusion in our policies, practices, and behaviours. We aim to build awareness and skills in this area, both internally and with our partners. Our commitment extends to creating a safe, positive work environment. For details on our Equity, Diversity & Inclusion commitment, please click here.

We’re committed to attracting and retaining passionate individuals to help create a healthier future. That’s why SickKids Foundation is looking for a new Associate Director, CRM Platforms & Data Governance
.

Description of the Position

The AD, CRM Platforms & Data Governance is accountable for the Foundation’s CRM and fundraising platform ecosystem, ensuring it operates as a reliable, secure, scalable, and well-governed enterprise product. This role leads CRM modernization, platform performance, donor and gift data governance, fundraising and payment capabilities, and the use of automation and AI to improve donor experience, operational efficiency, and business outcomes. As a hands-on technical leader, the Associate Director translates enterprise priorities into roadmaps, disciplined delivery, measurable outcomes, and continuous improvement. Working across IMT, Fundraising Operations, Finance, Digital, Marketing Technology, Cybersecurity, Privacy, and business partners, this role ensures platforms and data are aligned and sustainable.

Key Responsibilities

CRM Platform Product Ownership, Modernization, and Delivery

Own the CRM and fundraising platform ecosystem, including roadmap, backlog, releases, service performance, technical debt, adoption, and lifecycle management.
Lead CRM modernization and ongoing platform delivery through governed intake, prioritization, release planning, process redesign, configuration, migration, testing, cutover, stabilization, and transition to steady-state operations.
Translate enterprise priorities into clear delivery plans, measurable outcomes, and continuous improvement within the CRM and data governance portfolio.
Rationalize platforms and capabilities to reduce duplication, complexity, cost, customization, and vendor dependency.
Ensure CRM platforms and related capabilities comply with enterprise architecture, cybersecurity, privacy, data governance, and delivery standards.

Donor Data Governance and Platform Integrity

Establish and enforce governance for donor, gift, relationship, consent, preference, campaign, and engagement data maintained within CRM and fundraising platforms.
Define data ownership, stewardship, business rules, quality standards, retention requirements, and authoritative system-of-record responsibilities in partnership with business and technology teams.
Implement automated controls and remediation processes that improve data accuracy, completeness, consistency, traceability, and availability for reporting, analytics, automation, and AI.
Identify and manage material operational, technology, data, and delivery risks related to CRM platforms and donor data.
Support strong data governance practices that enable trusted decision-making, reliable reporting, and improved donor experience.

Fundraising Operations and Payment Capability

Own the technology capabilities supporting gift processing, recurring giving, pledges, donor servicing, transaction processing, receipting inputs, and reconciliation.
Partner with Fundraising Operations and Finance to maintain transaction integrity, auditability, service levels, and alignment across donor, gift, payment, and financial records.
Define CRM and reconciliation requirements for digital payment migrations led by Website & Digital Platforms.
Approve operational readiness for payment-related changes and assume steady-state payment platform ownership following transition.
Ensure fundraising and payment capabilities are scalable, secure, well-documented, and aligned with business requirements.

Automation, AI, and Operational Excellence

Identify and implement automation and AI opportunities across fundraising operations, donor servicing, data stewardship, workflow management, and platform administration.
Use automation and applied technical leadership to simplify work, accelerate delivery, improve data quality, and reduce reliance on incremental staffing.
Maintain reliable, secure, scalable, and recoverable platforms through effective monitoring, change control, incident management, documentation, and root-cause remediation.
Measure improvements in productivity, cycle time, quality, adoption, platform performance, and business value.
Drive continuous improvement through standardization, documentation, benchmarking, and disciplined operational practices.

Cross-Functional Collaboration and Enterprise Leadership

Partner across IMT and business functions to deliver Foundation-wide outcomes related to CRM modernization, fundraising operations, data governance, digital payments, analytics, automation, and AI.
Work closely with Fundraising Operations, Finance, Digital, Marketing Technology, Data Integration, Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Enterprise Architecture, and business partners to ensure cohesive platform delivery.
Provide clear direction, coaching, accountability, and development for team members and future leaders.
Support enterprise planning by providing accurate capacity, demand, risk, dependency, and value information to inform decisions.

Vendor and Financial Management

Manage vendors, contracts, licensing, service performance, and operational costs within delegated authority.
Maximize value from existing platform investments while identifying opportunities to reduce cost, duplication, and operational risk.
Monitor vendor performance, platform costs, and contract obligations to ensure value realization and sustainability.

Qualifications

While we know that for any job posting no one candidate will possess the qualifications being sought in equal measure, below is an outline of the qualifications we believe are important for a candidate to bring to the position or for the successful candidate to develop while in the role:

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Systems, Data Management, or a related field; a relevant advanced degree or certification is an asset.
Eight to ten years of progressive experience leading enterprise CRM, fundraising, constituent relationship, or comparable business platforms in a complex environment.
Demonstrated experience delivering a major CRM implementation, replacement, or modernization, including process redesign, data migration, testing, cutover, stabilization, and adoption.
Strong knowledge of platform product management, CRM configuration and releases, donor or customer data governance, gift processing, payment operations, and financial reconciliation.
Working knowledge of cloud platforms, integrations, application programming interfaces, data platforms, cybersecurity, privacy, and enterprise architecture principles.
Applied experience using automation and AI to improve workflows, data quality, analysis, productivity, and business outcomes.
Proven ability to translate enterprise priorities into roadmaps, delivery plans, measurable outcomes, and continuous improvement.
Strong vendor management, financial stewardship, risk management, communication, stakeholder engagement, and decision-making skills.
Experience leading, coaching, and developing team members with clarity, accountability, and a focus on enterprise outcomes.

We’re looking for a passionate individual who is interested in moving the dial and making a difference. We are an environment that looks to attract hardworking and committed people; people who want to challenge themselves and grow with a globally recognized brand that continues to change the world. If this describes you, consider joining our team. We look forward to reviewing your application.

Total Compensation Package

Expected Hiring Salary Range:
$99,297.00 – $124,121.00; with the ability to progress to a maximum of $142,739.00. To ensure fair and equitable pay at SickKids Foundation, placement on the salary range will be based on your years of experience, skills, and qualifications relevant to the Associate Director, CRM Platforms & Data Governance
.

To help you lead in the fight for kids’ health and to support your health, wellness, and career growth, in addition to competitive compensation, we offer a comprehensive benefit package including a flex benefit plan, tuition reimbursement, flexible work arrangements, pension plan and birth parent/parental top up – to name a few!

Position Status:
Permanent Full-Time

Hours:
Hybrid work model: minimum two days per week in-office, Tuesday and Wednesday.

Available To:
Internal and External Candidates

Available:
Immediately; this posting is for an existing vacancy.

Date Posted:
July 24, 2026.

Deadline:
August 7, 2026.

Screening and interviews may begin prior to the posting close date. We encourage early applications.

How to apply:
Please apply online by visiting our website: https://www.sickkidsfoundation.com/careersandvolunteers

Please note that automated tools, including artificial intelligence, may be used to support the pre-screening of applications as part of our recruitment process.

SickKids Foundation is committed to its people and the talents, capabilities, and perspectives they bring to our mission. We live that commitment by being open and accessible to all, by valuing and respecting every individual, and by equally supporting every employee. As an organization proud to have joined the BlackNorth Initiative’s CEO pledge, we uphold our commitment by inviting and encouraging individuals from diverse lived experiences from Black, Indigenous, communities of colour, people with disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ community and all candidates who may contribute to the further diversification of the Foundation’s community.

Candidates who require accommodation during the recruitment process should contact the People & Culture team at: recruitment@sickkidsfoundation.com

jobs.title: VP of Information Technology
jobs.description:
Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. Our diverse team of technologists have developed a high performance RISC-V CPU from scratch, and share a passion for AI and a deep desire to build the best AI platform possible. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities.

At Tenstorrent, we are building the next generation of AI and RISC-V compute. In this role as the VP of Information Technology you will be responsible for building and scaling the internal technology foundation that helps the company move fast, stay secure, and operate reliably across teams and geographies. This is a high-impact leadership role for someone who can own enterprise systems, infrastructure, security partnership, end-user experience, and global IT operations while helping the business scale with discipline.

This role is hybrid, based out of Austin, TX; Santa Clara, CA; or Toronto, ON.

We welcome candidates at various experience levels for this role. During the interview process, candidates will be assessed for the appropriate level, and offers will align with that level, which may differ from the one in this posting.

Who You Are

An experienced AI architect and innovation leader who treats IT as a business force multiplier, not just support.
Skilled at scaling IT infrastructure, enterprise applications, and security in fast-moving, high-growth environments.
A hands-on leader who sets clear visions, manages expenses, and builds team capabilities.
Clear, direct communicator capable of aligning technical teams and business stakeholders without unnecessary process.
Comfortable bridging executive strategy with tactical execution across corporate infrastructure and IT operations.

What We Need

Someone to rethink and evolve traditional IT services into new AI-driven capabilities and foundations.
An owner of the global IT strategy and operating model across all enterprise systems, infrastructure, and core business technology.
The ability to lead the roadmap for business applications, integrations, automation, and internal service delivery.
Partner with cross-functional leaders to ensure internal systems are effective, well-governed, and ready for scale while establishing clear operating rhythms and service standards.

What You Will Learn

How to strategically drive AI hardware and software development as an internal IT consumer.
How to accelerate traditional IT development timelines within a new, AI-driven ecosystem.
How to balance speed and operational rigor while supporting a global organization building AI hardware.
How to optimize cross-functional decisions, systems, and workflows in a technical, product-driven environment.

Compensation for all engineers at Tenstorrent ranges from $100k - $500k including base and variable compensation targets. Experience, skills, education, background and location all impact the actual offer made.

Tenstorrent offers a highly competitive compensation package and benefits, and we are an equal opportunity employer.

This offer of employment is contingent upon the applicant being eligible to access U.S. export-controlled technology. Due to U.S. export laws, including those codified in the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR), the Company is required to ensure compliance with these laws when transferring technology to nationals of certain countries (such as EAR Country Groups D:1, E1, and E2). These requirements apply to persons located in the U.S. and all countries outside the U.S. As the position offered will have direct and/or indirect access to information, systems, or technologies subject to these laws, the offer may be contingent upon your citizenship/permanent residency status or ability to obtain prior license approval from the U.S. Commerce Department or applicable federal agency. If employment is not possible due to U.S. export laws, any offer of employment will be rescinded.

jobs.title: Technology Audit, Assistant Vice President
jobs.description:
Who We Are Looking For

We are looking for a highly skilled and experienced Corporate Audit, Assistance Vice President to join our technology audit team. To succeed in this role, you need to have a deep understanding of technologies, technology processes and controls, industry standards and related risks for a global organization. You should also have strong knowledge of industry frameworks including COBIT and NIST CSF. You will be responsible for working closely with peers on a diverse global team to perform technology infrastructure, security, and horizontal audits. Collaboration with State Street’s technology organization is essential. In this role you will join a team that is focused on building leading practices, and you will have a functional reporting line to a Vice President of Technology Audit.

Why this role is important to us

The team you will be joining plays an important role in the overall success of the organization. Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. To make that happen we need teams like yours to help navigate employees and the organization as a whole. In your role you will strive for cutting-edge solutions, that are straightforward and scalable. You will help us build resilience and execute day to day deliverables at our best. Join us if making your mark in the financial services industry from day one is a challenge you are up for.

What You Will Be Responsible For

As Technology Audit Assistance Vice President, you will

Manage the planning, assessment, testing and reporting phases of technology audits and technology risk-focused validation activities.
Work as part of an international team, collaborating closely with global peers for resiliency, data, emerging tech, cyber, and third-party risk management and business audits.
Maintain a thorough knowledge of technology risks and changes in the regulatory environment.
Develop and maintain relationships with key stakeholders across the organization, including the Global Technology Services organization.
Communicate audit progress, findings and recommendations effectively to senior management.
Prepare and review audit work papers to ensure compliance with the division’s audit methodology.

What We Value

These skills will help you succeed in this role

Experience leading and supervising audit projects, preferably within the global financial services industry.
Proficiency in evaluating technology risks and testing internal controls while applying risk-based testing approaches.
Ability to prioritize multiple tasks, working independently and developing relationships with global stakeholders in a fast paced environment.
Strong communication, interpersonal, and leadership ability across all levels coupled with effective problem solving, conceptual thinking, quantitative and analytical skills.
Strong written and verbal communication, presentation, and technical writing skills.
Advanced project management skills.

Education & Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Business Administration or a related field.
5+ years of experience auditing information technologies, security or cyber risk management.
Audit or assurance experience working in the banking or financial services industry or other regulated industries.
Expertise in evaluating technology risks and the ability to develop and implement effective audit testing strategies with a strong understanding of regulatory compliance requirements for the banking industry.
Strong knowledge of technology risk management, including the latest trends, tools and techniques.
Strong knowledge in evaluating various horizontal IT and infrastructure technologies and platforms including networks, middleware, operating systems, change management, SDLC, cloud technologies and the ability to develop and implement effective audit coverage strategies.
Relevant certifications, such as CISSP, CISA, CISM, or CIA are highly preferred.

Additional Requirements

May require travel up to 10% of the year

Salary Range

$80,000 - $140,000 Annual

The range quoted above applies to the role in the primary location specified. If the candidate would ultimately work outside of the primary location above, the applicable range could differ.

Employees are eligible to participate in State Street’s comprehensive benefits program, which includes: our retirement savings plan (401K) with company match; insurance coverage including basic life, medical, dental, vision, long-term disability, and other optional additional coverages; paid-time off including vacation, sick leave, short term disability, and family care responsibilities; access to our Employee Assistance Program; incentive compensation including eligibility for annual performance-based awards (excluding certain sales roles subject to sales incentive plans); and, eligibility for certain tax advantaged savings plans.

For a full overview, visit https://hrportal.ehr.com/statestreet/Home .

About State Street

Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are essential to our continued success.

We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. As an essential partner in our shared success, you’ll benefit from inclusive development opportunities, flexible work-life support, paid volunteer days, and vibrant employee networks that keep you connected to what matters most. Join us in shaping the future.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we consider all qualified applicants for all positions without regard to race, creed, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, age, disability, genetic information, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, citizenship, marital status, domestic partnership or civil union status, familial status, military and veteran status, and other characteristics protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Director, Financial Planning & Analysis
jobs.description:
We're Hiring!

We are looking for a Director, Financial Planning & Analysis
to join our team.

This role will lead the financial planning process, analyze performance, provide strategic insights, and support strategic planning and corporate development for Andean. The position will work closely with the CFO and senior leadership to drive financial strategy, optimize costs, support business growth initiatives, and ensure robust financial modeling, data-driven decision-making and effective financial reporting.

Location:
Toronto, Canada – On-site.
This position requires extensive travel to Andean's mine sites in Bolivia and California, USA.

Responsibilities:

Financial Planning, Budgeting & Forecasting

Lead the annual budgeting process and long-term financial planning for all aspects of Andean, coordinating inputs across departments and mine sites
Coordinate, consolidate, and deliver the Annual Plan, Rolling Latest Best Estimate (RLBE), and other periodic forecasts
Maintain an effective planning calendar with key dates and deliverables for all functional areas
Own and administer the corporate planning process within Oracle Hyperion / EPM, including maintaining planning models, hierarchies, scenarios, and reports, and driving continuous improvement of the system
Develop flexible tools, templates, and process improvements that support timely, accurate consolidation of corporate planning and reporting schedules

Financial Modeling & Analysis

Build and maintain revenue, cost, and cash flow models and valuations for the company and its assets; run scenario and sensitivity analyses
Analyze financial trends, commodity market conditions, and operational performance to inform strategic decision-making
Model long-term growth and identify the business drivers that influence it
Assess risks and opportunities associated with commodity pricing, operational efficiency, and capital expenditures

Performance Reporting & Business Partnering

Prepare the monthly financial performance package, KPI reporting, and financial dashboard; develop KPIs and metrics to assess company performance
Lead monthly financial review meetings with each department, reporting actuals against budget and reviewing variances and corrective actions
Prepare the monthly headcount actual-to-budget variance report and related forecasts
Conduct cost analyses, provide commentary on cost centre findings, and recommend initiatives to improve efficiency and profitability
Provide actionable analysis and recommendations to senior leadership, explaining actual performance against budget and forecast
Oversee the preparation of management reports and presentations; support ad hoc analysis as required

Strategy & Corporate Development

Partner with the executive team to develop Andean's medium- and long-term financial and strategic plans
Support M&A activity, capital investment decisions, and financial due diligence, including post-merger integration and monitoring acquired assets against their expected value and ROI
Identify business issues, propose solutions, and support their implementation

Team Leadership

Manage, coach, and develop one direct report based in Mexico, setting clear objectives, reviewing deliverables, and supporting professional growth
Provide functional leadership and direction to the mine asset finance and planning teams, which report indirectly to this role; set standards, review deliverables, and ensure consistency and quality of planning, forecasting, and reporting across all sites
Build strong working relationships with site-based finance and planning teams through regular engagement and extensive travel to the mine sites

Qualifications and Skills:

Bachelor’s Degree from a recognized University or College in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or Mining Engineer or related field. 
Master’s Degree - MBA in Accounting or Finance or Chartered Financial Analyst is preferred
Expert level experience in Excel, including the ability to write macros
Experience using Power BI or other financial analysis experience
10+ years of finance, financial planning, corporate development or accounting experience with a focus on Financial Planning and Analysis within the mining industry
Excellent verbal, written communication and presentation skills.
Strong MS office skills and financial systems applications.
Ability to work in a highly matrixed and geographically diverse business environment.
Ability to work within a team and as an individual contributor in a fast-paced, changing environment.
Hands-on experience with Oracle Hyperion / EPM planning applications is required, including building and maintaining budgets, forecasts, and reports within the platform
Ability to leverage and/or engage others to accomplish projects
Spanish speaker is a plus     

If your background and expertise align with this opportunity, we invite you to apply and become part of Andean Precious Metals. We look forward to hearing from you!

jobs.title: Director, PathWise Actuarial Implementation and AI-Enabled Process Transformation
jobs.description:
The Life Solutions division at Aon is seeking a Director to lead large-scale PathWise implementation projects. This role also supports AI-enabled process transformation initiatives for life and annuity insurers across North America. This client-facing role combines actuarial expertise, implementation leadership, and technology-enabled transformation to help insurers modernize modelling, reporting, workflow automation, AI-enabled systems, and operational workflows.

The Director will work within Aon Life Solutions, part of Aon’s Reinsurance Strategy and Technology Group to translate business needs into practical implementation plans, scalable operating models, and measurable delivery outcomes. This role will be based in Canada.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in Canada. This role is not eligible for sponsorship, and we are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa or work permit.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What The Day Will Look Like

Implementation and Client Delivery

Lead and support large-scale PathWise implementation projects for life and annuity insurers across North America.
Handle key implementation workstreams, including model migration, data integration, testing, reconciliation, workflow design, documentation, training, and production deployment.
Translate client business objectives and current-state processes into clear delivery plans, target-state solutions, and implementation roadmaps.
Develop and migrate actuarial models and production processes for valuation, pricing, financial reporting, capital, ALM, and risk management use cases.
Support delivery governance, issue resolution, risk management, collaborator communication, post-implementation stabilization, and client knowledge transfer.

AI-Enabled Process Transformation and Innovation

Identify, prioritize, and continuously refine opportunities to use automation and AI-enabled capabilities to improve actuarial modelling, reporting, reconciliation, documentation, and analysis processes across the PathWise lifecycle.
Collaborate closely with the PathWise AI and development teams to translate business difficulties into clear AI use cases, feature requests, and improvements.
Help clients redesign legacy actuarial workflows into more efficient, scalable, governed, and technology-enabled operating models.
Contribute to reusable implementation assets, process transformation playbooks, documentation templates, workflow designs, and AI-enabled delivery accelerators.
Lead or support pilots of new PathWise AI features, capturing user feedback and performance metrics, and consolidating insights into actionable recommendations for the PathWise AI roadmap
Promote responsible and controlled use of AI-enabled capabilities, including review, validation, traceability, documentation, and governance, and contribute to standard guidance on AI-enabled workflows

Business Development and Market Support

Support PathWise growth in the North American life and annuity market through client solutioning, demonstrations (including AI-enabled capabilities), proposals, implementation estimates, and project planning.
Partner with senior leaders in client discussions on actuarial modernization, implementation strategy, process automation, AI-enabled transformation, and business value.
Develop proof-of-concept materials and presentations on PathWise capabilities, implementation guidelines, and emerging insurance industry issues.
Develop and share case studies, training materials, and thought leadership that showcase successful AI-enabled PathWise use cases and evolving capabilities

How this opportunity is different

PathWise is Aon’s high-performance actuarial software platform, enabling insurers to model liabilities, assets, capital, and related business processes with speed, transparency, flexibility, and control. The platform supports modern actuarial modelling, scenario analysis, financial reporting, ALM, risk management, and enterprise-scale production processes.

In this role, you will help clients migrate models and processes into PathWise, improve actuarial production workflows, and apply automation and AI-enabled capabilities across requirements, model development, testing, reconciliation, documentation, workflow monitoring, and reporting. You will also help identify new AI applications within PathWise, develop improvements with the PathWise AI team, and promote adoption of emerging capabilities across client and internal teams.

Skills And Experience That Will Lead To Success

10+ years of experience in life insurance, life reinsurance, actuarial consulting, financial technology, actuarial modelling, or enterprise platform implementation.
Experience with valuation, pricing, ALM, hedging, capital, financial reporting, risk management, model governance, or related actuarial functions.
Experience supporting or leading implementation, modernization, migration, or transformation projects within actuarial, finance, risk, or insurance technology environments.
Solid understanding of life and annuity products, reserves, capital, financial reporting, ALM, and risk management.
Practical experience with actuarial modelling platforms, model migration, data transformation, testing, reconciliation, workflow automation, documentation, and production process improvement.
Experience identifying and shaping AI-enabled transformation opportunities (e.g., automation, analytics, AI-assisted development, or generative AI applications) in actuarial or financial services processes, including working with development teams to refine and implement new features
Knowledge of programming, data workflows, Python, APIs, cloud infrastructure, or automation concepts is preferred.
Comfort acting as a bridge between actuarial users and technical AI / software teams, including providing structured feedback on prototypes and helping define success metrics and acceptance criteria for new capabilities
Strong project delivery, customer management, communication, and team leadership skills.
Member of the Society of Actuaries, Canadian Institute of Actuaries, or equivalent actuarial organization preferred.

Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate .
